This module is a pre-completion checklist for time series work: a short set of checks to run before calling a time series task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any time series bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Validate time series outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Prefer the simplest time series approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen time series approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. When time series guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Before starting time series work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Document any non-obvious time series decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Prefer explicit, readable time series solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. Keep time series changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. Check that time series terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
11. Re-check edge cases relevant to time series (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated time series concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop time series edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic time series advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about time series over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
